2. `kinnoo inspect <archive.kno>` reads manifest from inside the archive without extracting the full archive
3. Output is human-readable formatted text (not raw YAML)
4. Missing optional fields are omitted from output (not shown as "None" or empty)
5. Invalid manifest produces a clear error (reuses feature1 validator)
6. `kinnoo inspect` without arguments prints usage help

#### feature12 — Local Registry (`kinnoo publish`, `kinnoo install <name>`, `kinnoo list`, `kinnoo search`)

Implement a local registry at `~/.kinnoo/registry/` where agents can be published by name/version and installed by name. `kinnoo publish` publishes locally by default with a `--local` flag for explicitness. Code is structured so switching the default to remote in the future is straightforward. Version is determined by the `version` field in the agent's `kinnoo.yaml`.

**ACs:**
1. `kinnoo publish <archive.kno>` extracts the version from the archive's `kinnoo.yaml` and copies the archive to `~/.kinnoo/registry/<name>/<version>/`
2. `kinnoo publish <archive.kno> --local` does the same (explicit local flag)
3. `kinnoo install <name>` resolves the latest version from local registry and installs it (no network)
4. `kinnoo install <name>==<version>` installs a specific version from local registry
5. `kinnoo list` displays all locally published agents with name, version, and description
6. `kinnoo search <query>` filters the local registry by name/description substring match
7. Publishing the same name+version twice produces a clear error: "Version X.Y.Z of \<name\> already exists in registry" (no silent overwrite)
8. `kinnoo install <file.kno>` (file path) continues to work as before (V1 behavior preserved)
9. Publish logic is behind an abstraction (e.g., `RegistryBackend` interface or similar) so swapping local for remote backend is a minimal change

Template Types\n\nDefined in [src/kinnoo/templates.py](src/kinnoo/templates.py):\n\n| Template | &#96;run.py&#96; Pattern | Requirements | API Key |\n|----------|------------------|--------------|---------|\n| **Default** (no framework) | &#96;asyncio.run(main(input))&#96; → prints hello world | Empty | None |\n| **Gemini** | &#96;google.genai.Client&#96; → &#96;generate_content()&#96; with &#96;gemini-2.5-flash-lite&#96; | &#96;google-genai&#96; | &#96;GOOGLE_API_KEY&#96; |\n| **ChatGPT** | &#96;openai.AsyncOpenAI&#96; → &#96;chat.completions.create()&#96; with &#96;gpt-5-nano&#96; | &#96;openai&#96; | &#96;OPENAI_API_KEY&#96; |\n| **Claude Chat** | &#96;anthropic.AsyncAnthropic&#96; → &#96;messages.create()&#96; with &#96;claude-sonnet-4&#96; | &#96;anthropic&#96; | &#96;ANTHROPIC_API_KEY&#96; |\n\nAll templates use async boilerplate (&#96;asyncio.run()&#96;) for compatibility with async-first frameworks.\n\nThe default &#96;kinnoo.yaml&#96; template generates:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;yaml\nname: {name}\nversion: 0.1.0\nentrypoint: run.py\nruntime:\n  language: python\n  version: \"&gt;=3.10\"\n  type: one-shot\ndependencies: []\ninputs:\n  type: text\noutputs:\n  type: text\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n### 5. Existing Support for Data Files, Vector Stores, External Services\n\n**Currently: None implemented.** All of these are documented as V2+ concepts in [notes/techlead-agent-notes.md](notes/techlead-agent-notes.md):\n\n- **Memory/context schema** (conceptual only): &#96;memory.type&#96; with values &#96;none&#96;, &#96;in-process&#96;, &#96;vector&#96;, &#96;key-value&#96;, &#96;episodic&#96;. Vector stores would reference backends like pinecone, chroma, weaviate, pgvector, qdrant with &#96;embedding_model&#96; and &#96;collection&#96; fields.\n- **Storage/RAG** (conceptual only): &#96;storage.files&#96; for local/S3/GCS file access and &#96;storage.vector_stores&#96; for vector DB connections. Both use &#96;env.*&#96; references for secrets and declare &#96;permissions&#96;.\n- **Tools/MCP/databases** (conceptual only): &#96;tools&#96; section supporting &#96;builtin&#96;, &#96;mcp&#96;, &#96;database&#96;, and &#96;http&#96; tool types with auth via &#96;env.*&#96; references.\n- **Service mocks** (conceptual only): Layer 4 of the portability roadmap — &#96;fakeredis&#96;, SQLite shims, &#96;moto&#96; for S3. Deferred.\n\nThe V2 plan explicitly states: *\"Memory/storage/composition manifest fields — too early for V2.\"* These are V3+ items.\n\n---\n\n### 6. V2 Feature Plan Summary\n\nDocumented across [notes/phase2-plan-opus-4-6.md](notes/phase2-plan-opus-4-6.md), [notes/phase2-plan-opus-4-6-followup.md](notes/phase2-plan-opus-4-6-followup.md), [notes/phase2-plan-opus-4-6-featureI now have comprehensive context. Here is the full research summary:\n\n---\n\n## Kinnoo Project Research Summary\n\n### 1. What Kinnoo Is\n\nKinnoo is a **developer platform for packaging, sharing, and running AI agents** — analogous to Docker for containerized apps or npm for JavaScript packages. The core idea: turn a complex, framework-dependent AI agent into a **portable, reproducible, installable unit** that any developer can run with one command.\n\n**Vision** (from [vision.md](vision.md)): A platform where developers can publish, version-control, and share agents across frameworks (CrewAI, LangChain, PydanticAI, etc.), with security and human control as priorities.\n\n**Tagline**: *\"Package any agent. Share it. Run it — with its tools, keys, and connections ready.\"*\n\n---\n\n### 2. Full Manifest Schema (Current V1)\n\nDefined in [src/kinnoo/schema.py](src/kinnoo/schema.py) and documented in [docs/manifest-schema-reference.md](docs/manifest-schema-reference.md):\n\n| Field | Required | Type | Constraints |\n|-------|----------|------|-------------|\n| &#96;name&#96; | yes | string | Lowercase alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores. Must start with letter/digit. Pattern: &#96;^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-_]*$&#96; |\n| &#96;version&#96; | yes | string | Valid semver (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, optional pre-release/build metadata) |\n| &#96;entrypoint&#96; | yes | string | File path to the main script (e.g., &#96;run.py&#96;) |\n| &#96;runtime.language&#96; | yes | string | e.g., &#96;\"python\"&#96; |\n| &#96;runtime.version&#96; | yes | string | Version constraint (e.g., &#96;\"&gt;=3.10\"&#96;) |\n| &#96;runtime.type&#96; | yes | string | Only &#96;\"one-shot\"&#96; supported in V1 |\n| &#96;dependencies&#96; | yes | list[string] | Pip package names; can be empty &#96;[]&#96; |\n| &#96;inputs.type&#96; | yes | list (normalized) | e.g., &#96;[\"text\"]&#96;. Strings auto-normalized to single-element lists |\n| &#96;outputs.type&#96; | yes | list (normalized) | Same normalization as inputs |\n| &#96;framework&#96; | no | string | Optional metadata (e.g., &#96;\"langchain\"&#96;, &#96;\"crewai\"&#96;) — not used at runtime |\n\n**Normalization logic** (also in [schema.py](src/kinnoo/schema.py)):\n- &#96;normalize_manifest_defaults()&#96; — injects defaults for &#96;dependencies&#96;, &#96;inputs&#96;, &#96;outputs&#96; if missing\n- &#96;normalize_type_field()&#96; — converts &#96;type: text&#96; (string) to &#96;type: [\"text\"]&#96; (list) for inputs/outputs\n\n**Validation constants:**\n- &#96;SUPPORTED_RUNTIME_TYPES = [\"one-shot\"]&#96;\n- &#96;SEMVER_PATTERN&#96; — full semver regex with pre-release/build metadata support\n- &#96;NAME_PATTERN = r\"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-_]*$\"&#96;\n\n---\n\n### 3. Pack / Install / Run Lifecycle\n\n**&#96;kinnoo init &lt;name&gt; [--framework &lt;fw&gt;]&#96;** ([init_command.py](src/kinnoo/init_command.py)):\n- Creates agent directory with canonical structure: &#96;kinnoo.yaml&#96;, &#96;run.py&#96;, &#96;requirements.txt&#96;, &#96;README.md&#96;, &#96;tools/&#96;, &#96;prompts/&#96;\n- Supports &#96;--framework&#96; flag: &#96;gemini&#96;, &#96;chatgpt&#96;, &#96;claude-chat&#96; — generates framework-specific &#96;run.py&#96; with LLM API boilerplate\n- Without &#96;--framework&#96;, generates a vanilla hello-world agent\n\n**&#96;kinnoo run &lt;agent-dir&gt; \"&lt;input&gt;\"&#96;** (inline in [cli.py](src/kinnoo/cli.py)):\n1. Validates &#96;kinnoo.yaml&#96; exists\n2. Parses manifest to get entrypoint\n3. Creates &#96;.venv/&#96; in agent directory if not exists\n4. Installs &#96;requirements.txt&#96; into venv\n5. Executes: &#96;python &lt;entrypoint&gt; \"&lt;input&gt;\"&#96; inside venv\n6. Pipes stdout/stderr to terminal, propagates exit code\n\n**&#96;kinnoo pack &lt;agent-dir&gt;&#96;** ([cli.py](src/kinnoo/cli.py) + [pack_command.py](src/kinnoo/pack_command.py)):\n1. Validates manifest via [validator.py](src/kinnoo/validator.py)\n2. Checks entrypoint and requirements.txt exist\n3. Builds wheel files for all dependencies using &#96;pip wheel -r requirements.txt --no-deps&#96; (**known issue: no transitive deps**)\n4. Creates &#96;.kno&#96; archive (ZIP format) containing: &#96;kinnoo.yaml&#96;, entrypoint, &#96;requirements.txt&#96;, &#96;wheels/*.whl&#96;\n\n**&#96;kinnoo install &lt;archive.kno&gt; [target-dir]&#96;** (inline in [cli.py](src/kinnoo/cli.py)):\n1. Validates &#96;.kno&#96; extension and file existence\n2. Extracts ZIP to target directory (collision handling with &#96;--force&#96;)\n3. Validates extracted &#96;kinnoo.yaml&#96; via validator\n4. Creates &#96;.venv/&#96; and installs wheel files from &#96;wheels/&#96; directory\n5. Agent is immediately runnable with &#96;kinnoo run&#96;\n\n---\n\n### 4. Template Types\n\nDefined in [src/kinnoo/templates.py](src/kinnoo/templates.py):\n\n| Template | Framework | &#96;run.py&#96; Pattern | Requirements |\n|----------|-----------|-----------------|--------------|\n| Default | None | &#96;asyncio.run(main(input))&#96; → prints hello world | Empty |\n| Gemini | &#96;google-genai&#96; | Async call to &#96;genai.Client.models.generate_content&#96; | &#96;google-genai&#96; |\n| ChatGPT | &#96;openai&#96; | Async call to &#96;openai.AsyncOpenAI.chat.completions.create&#96; | &#96;openai&#96; |\n| Claude | &#96;anthropic&#96; | Async call to &#96;anthropic.AsyncAnthropic.messages.create&#96; | &#96;anthropic&#96; |\n\nAll templates share the same &#96;kinnoo.yaml&#96; structure (only &#96;run.py&#96;, requirements, and README differ). The generated &#96;kinnoo.yaml&#96; template:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;yaml\nname: {name}\nversion: 0.1.0\nentrypoint: run.py\nruntime:\n  language: python\n  version: \"&gt;=3.10\"\n  type: one-shot\ndependencies: []\ninputs:\n  type: text\noutputs:\n  type: text\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n### 5. Existing Support for Data Files, Vector Stores, External Services\n\n**Currently: None implemented.** All of these are documented as future V2+ plans in [notes/techlead-agent-notes.md](notes/techlead-agent-notes.md):\n\n**Proposed memory/context schema** (not implemented):\n&#96;&#96;&#96;yaml\nmemory:\n  type: none | in-process | vector | key-value | episodic\n  backend: pinecone | chroma | weaviate | pgvector | qdrant\n  embedding_model: text-embedding-3-small\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Proposed storage/vector store schema** (not implemented):\n&#96;&#96;&#96;yaml\nstorage:\n  files:\n    - name: documents\n      type: local | s3 | gcs | azure-blob\n      path: ./data/\n      permissions: read\n  vector_stores:\n    - name: product_catalog\n      type: pinecone | chroma | weaviate\n      embedding_model: text-embedding-3-small\n      connection: env.PINECONE_API_KEY\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Proposed tools/services schema** (not implemented):\n&#96;&#96;&#96;yaml\ntools:\n  - name: github\n    type: mcp\n    server: github/github-mcp-server\n    auth: env.GITHUB_TOKEN\n  - name: customer_db\n    type: database\n    engine: postgres\n    connection: env.DATABASE_URL\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Current V2 plan approach:** Rather than building these schemas directly, V2 uses a **pass-through model** — &#96;env_vars&#96; in the manifest declares what environment variables an agent needs (API keys, connection strings), and Kinnoo injects them. The agent's own code handles the actual connections. This avoids Kinnoo needing to understand/manage vector stores, databases, etc.\n\n---\n\n### 6. V2 Feature Plan Summary\n\nFrom [notes/phases/phase2-plan-features.md](notes/phases/phase2-plan-features.md) — **26 features (feature7–feature32)** organized in 6 tiers:\n\n**Tier 1 — Foundation (tech debt):**\n- **feature7:** CLI refactor — extract install to &#96;install_command.py&#96;, add &#96;--version&#96;\n- **feature8:** Packaging robustness — transitive deps, canonical zip format, fallback on failed wheels\n- **feature9:** Manifest V2 extensions — &#96;description&#96;, &#96;author&#96;, &#96;license&#96;, &#96;env_vars&#96; (list[string]), &#96;runtime.type&#96; as list supporting &#96;[\"one-shot\", \"interactive\", \"mcp-server\"]&#96;\n\n**Tier 2 — Core:**\n- **feature10:** Env var / secret management — resolve from env → .env file → interactive prompt (masked). **Absolute rule: secret values never displayed/logged**\n- **feature11:** &#96;kinnoo inspect&#96; command — display manifest metadata from dir or archive\n- **feature12:** Local registry — &#96;kinnoo publish&#96;, &#96;kinnoo install &lt;name&gt;&#96;, &#96;kinnoo list&#96;, &#96;kinnoo search&#96;. Registry at &#96;~/.kinnoo/registry/&#96;. Abstracted backend for future remote swap\n\n**Tier 3 — One-Shot Framework Templates:**\n- **feature13–15:** PydanticAI, LangGraph, Agno one-shot templates via &#96;--framework&#96;\n\n**Tier 4 — Preflight &amp; Trust:**\n- **feature16:** &#96;--preflight&#96; flag on &#96;kinnoo run&#96; — checks Python version, env vars, entrypoint, deps\n- **feature17:** Trust baseline — install summary/confirmation, unverified source warning, run trace logging (no secrets)\n\n**Tier 5 — Interactive Mode:**\n- **feature18:** Core interactive runtime (&#96;--interactive&#96; flag, REPL loop, &#96;/exit&#96;, &#96;/clear&#96;, transcript)\n- **feature19–24:** Per-framework interactive templates (Gemini, ChatGPT, Claude, PydanticAI, LangGraph, Agno) via &#96;--mode interactive&#96;\n\n**Tier 6 — MCP Support:**\n- **feature25:** MCP server runtime (&#96;runtime.type: mcp-server&#96;, long-running process)\n- **feature26:** MCP server init template (&#96;--mcp-server&#96; flag)\n- **feature27–32:** Per-framework GitHub MCP templates (&#96;--mcp github&#96; flag, GitHub only in V2)\n\n---\n\n### 7. Key Design Constraints &amp; Principles\n\n1. **Black-box execution model:** The agent is an opaque process. Kinnoo doesn't know/care what framework runs inside. &#96;python run.py \"&lt;input&gt;\"&#96; is the universal contract. This is the core architectural decision.\n\n2. **Framework-agnostic by design:** Kinnoo is the **Host** (infrastructure/environment manager), not the **Client** (tool integrator). Frameworks handle MCP clients, tool calls, conversation state — Kinnoo provides venv isolation, secret injection, and process management.\n\n3. **Pass-through secret model:** Kinnoo declares required env vars in the manifest and injects them into the subprocess. It never interprets, stores, or logs their values. The agent code handles actual API connections.\n\n4. **No session context in Kinnoo:** Conversation history is managed entirely by the framework inside &#96;run.py&#96;. Kinnoo provides the REPL shell for interactive mode; the template handles context.\n\n5. **&#96;runtime.type&#96; as list:** Allows agents to support multiple modes (e.g., &#96;[\"one-shot\", \"interactive\"]&#96;). Normalized like &#96;inputs.type&#96;/&#96;outputs.type&#96;.\n\n6. **Security stance:** V1/V2 are warning-based (display deps before install, warn on untrusted sources). Full sandboxing deferred to V3+. Secret values must never appear in any output, log, or code path.\n\n7. **Graduated isolation:** venv → sandbox → container. Docker is an escape hatch, not the default. Most agents need reproducible Python environments, not full containerization.\n\n8. **Registry abstraction:** Local registry in V2 with backend interface, so swapping to remote in V3 is minimal work.\n\n9. **V3 public release gates:** PyPI publication, documentation site, cross-platform CI, remote registry, &#96;kinnoo test&#96;, archive integrity/checksums, error UX polish, example agent gallery.\n\n10. **Additive schema changes only:** All V2+ manifest fields are optional — V1 manifests remain valid forever."
}

 The user is asking me to think about how Kinnoo (an AI agent packaging/distribution tool) could support RAG-based LLM agents. Let me first gather context about what Kinnoo currently does and its architecture, then think through what RAG agents would need. Now I have comprehensive context about Kinnoo. Let me think through what it would take to support RAG-based LLM agents. This is a planning/thinking exercise, not implementation.

RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) agents have specific requirements beyond simple one-shot or interactive agents:

1. **Data/Document Storage**: RAG agents need access to documents (PDFs, text files, web pages, etc.) that form their knowledge base
2. **Vector Store**: They need a vector database (Chroma, Pinecone, Weaviate, FAISS, Qdrant, etc.) to store embeddings


3. **Embedding Model**: They need an embedding model to convert documents to vectors
4. **Retrieval Pipeline**: Query → embed → search → retrieve relevant chunks → augment prompt → generate
5. **Indexing Pipeline**: Documents → chunk → embed → store in vector DB
6. **Potentially Large Data**: Knowledge bases can be gigabytes

From Kinnoo's perspective, the main challenge is maintaining the black-box execution model while enabling RAG agents to be packaged and shared. The biggest hurdles are figuring out how to make knowledge bases portable—they could be massive—and handling pre-built vector indices that need to travel with the agent.

Beyond that, there's the question of embedding model access, whether indices should be static or refreshed dynamically, and the storage overhead that vector databases demand. I should map out different approaches and what each one would need.Great question — this is a natural evolution of Kinnoo's capabilities. Let me lay out the design thinking.

---

## Plan: RAG Agent Support in Kinnoo (V3 Outline)

### The Core Challenge

RAG agents differ from simple one-shot/interactive agents in that they depend on a **data pipeline**: documents → chunking → embedding → vector store → retrieval → generation. This introduces new concerns Kinnoo doesn't currently handle:

| Concern | Current Kinnoo | RAG Requirement |
|---------|---------------|-----------------|
| Data files | Not packaged | Knowledge base (PDFs, text, CSVs) must be available |
| Vector store | N/A | Embeddings must be queryable at runtime |
| Embedding model | N/A | Needed for indexing and/or query-time embedding |
| Index lifecycle | N/A | Build once? Rebuild on install? Update dynamically? |
| Archive size | Small (code + wheels) | Potentially gigabytes (docs + index) |
| External services | `env_vars` pass-through | May need Pinecone/Weaviate/Postgres connections |

### Design Philosophy: Stay Black-Box

The key insight: **Kinnoo should not become a RAG framework.** LangChain, LlamaIndex, PydanticAI, and others already handle the retrieval pipeline. Kinnoo's job is to ensure the agent's data and dependencies are **portable, reproducible, and runnable** — the same role it plays for code and secrets today.

This means Kinnoo needs to solve **packaging and lifecycle** problems, not retrieval problems.

---

### Proposed Approach: Three Tiers of RAG Support

#### Tier A — Embedded RAG (Simplest, V3 MVP)

**What:** The entire knowledge base and vector index are bundled inside the `.kno` archive. The agent uses a local/embedded vector store (FAISS, ChromaDB local, SQLite-VSS).

**Manifest additions:**
```yaml
# New optional section
data:
  - name: knowledge-base
    path: ./data/docs/          # Bundled in archive
    description: "Product documentation corpus"
  - name: vector-index
    path: ./data/chroma_db/     # Pre-built index, bundled
    description: "Pre-built ChromaDB index"

# New optional section
lifecycle:
  post_install: scripts/build_index.py   # Run after kinnoo install
  pre_run: scripts/check_index.py        # Validate before each run
```

**What Kinnoo does:**
1. `kinnoo pack` includes `data/` directories listed in manifest (with size warnings)
2. `kinnoo install` extracts data, optionally runs `post_install` script (e.g., rebuild index from bundled docs)
3. `kinnoo run` passes through — agent code handles retrieval internally
4. New `kinnoo init --framework <fw> --mode rag` template that scaffolds a RAG agent with embedded ChromaDB

**Pros:** Fully portable, no external dependencies, works offline
**Cons:** Archive size (large corpora = large `.kno`), stale indices, no dynamic updates

**Changes required:**
- Schema: add `data` section (list of named paths), `lifecycle` hooks
- Pack: include data directories, enforce size limits/warnings
- Install: run lifecycle hooks in venv
- Templates: RAG-specific templates per framework
- Validation: verify data paths exist, lifecycle scripts exist

---

#### Tier B — Connected RAG (External Vector Store)

**What:** The agent connects to an external vector store (Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant Cloud, Postgres+pgvector). Documents may or may not be bundled — the index lives remotely.

**Manifest additions (extends Tier A):**
```yaml
env_vars:
  - PINECONE_API_KEY
  - PINECONE_INDEX_URL
  - OPENAI_API_KEY          # For embeddings

services:
  - name: vector-store
    type: pinecone | weaviate | qdrant | pgvector
    connection: env.PINECONE_INDEX_URL
    auth: env.PINECONE_API_KEY
    description: "Product catalog embeddings"

data:
  - name: raw-docs
    path: ./data/docs/
    optional: true           # May not be needed if index is pre-built remotely
```

**What Kinnoo does:**
1. `kinnoo install` + preflight validates that required env vars and service connections are available
2. `kinnoo run --preflight` checks service reachability (HTTP ping to vector store endpoint)
3. Kinnoo injects connection secrets — agent code handles the actual retrieval
4. Optional: `kinnoo index <agent-dir>` command to run the indexing pipeline on demand

**Pros:** No archive bloat, production-ready, supports large-scale corpora
**Cons:** Not portable offline, requires service setup, sharing agents means sharing infrastructure

**Changes required:**
- Schema: add `services` section (type, connection, auth references)
- Preflight: service health checks (TCP/HTTP)
- CLI: optional `kinnoo index` command for explicit indexing
- Trust: warn about external service connections during install

---

#### Tier C — Hybrid RAG (Data Reference + Build)

**What:** The agent bundles raw documents but the vector index is built on install or on first run. Supports both local and remote vector stores.

**Manifest additions:**
```yaml
data:
  - name: knowledge-base
    source: ./data/docs/        # Bundled raw documents
    format: pdf | markdown | text | csv
  - name: knowledge-base-remote
    source: https://example.com/docs.tar.gz  # Downloaded on install
    checksum: sha256:abc123...

lifecycle:
  post_install: scripts/build_index.py
  
index:
  strategy: build-on-install | build-on-first-run | pre-built
  script: scripts/index.py
  vector_store: local | env.VECTOR_STORE_URL
  embedding_model: text-embedding-3-small
  embedding_provider: env.OPENAI_API_KEY
```

**What Kinnoo does:**
1. `kinnoo pack` bundles raw docs, includes indexing script
2. `kinnoo install` downloads remote data sources (with checksum verification), runs indexing
3. `kinnoo run` checks index freshness, optionally rebuilds
4. `kinnoo index <agent-dir> [--rebuild]` explicitly triggers indexing

**Pros:** Maximum flexibility, reproducible from source docs, supports both local and cloud
**Cons:** Most complex, install time increases (embedding documents), requires embedding API access

---

### Implementation Roadmap (V3 Features)

| Feature | Tier | Description | Dependencies |
|---------|------|-------------|--------------|
| `data` manifest section | A | Declare data directories to bundle | Schema V3 |
| Data bundling in `kinnoo pack` | A | Include data dirs in `.kno`, size warnings | `data` schema |
| `lifecycle` hooks | A | `post_install`, `pre_run` scripts | None |
| RAG template: LangChain + ChromaDB | A | `--framework langchain --mode rag` | Interactive templates (V2) |
| RAG template: LlamaIndex + FAISS | A | `--framework llamaindex --mode rag` | New framework support |
| RAG template: PydanticAI + ChromaDB | A | `--framework pydanticai --mode rag` | PydanticAI template (V2) |
| `services` manifest section | B | Declare external service dependencies | `env_vars` (V2) |
| Service preflight checks | B | TCP/HTTP reachability checks | Preflight (V2) |
| `kinnoo index` command | B/C | Run indexing pipeline on demand | `lifecycle` hooks |
| Remote data sources | C | Download + checksum verification on install | `data` schema |
| `index` manifest section | C | Declare indexing strategy and config | `lifecycle` hooks |
| Index freshness checks | C | Detect stale indices, auto-rebuild | `index` schema |

### Key Design Decisions to Make

1. **Archive size limits:** Should Kinnoo enforce a max `.kno` size? Warn at 100MB, hard limit at 1GB? Or just warn?

2. **Lifecycle hook sandboxing:** `post_install` scripts run arbitrary code. This is a trust concern — Tier B/C of V2's trust features need to land first.

3. **Embedding cost:** Building an index on install requires API calls (and money). Kinnoo should estimate and warn: "This agent will make ~500 embedding API calls during install. Continue?"

4. **LlamaIndex as a first-class framework:** RAG is LlamaIndex's core competency. Should it be added as a framework in V2 (templates only) to prepare for V3 RAG support?

5. **Data versioning:** If a corpus changes, the agent version should change. Should Kinnoo hash data directories and include in the manifest checksum?

6. **`--mode rag` vs. separate flag:** Is `--mode rag` the right UX, or should it be `--rag` since RAG is orthogonal to one-shot/interactive (you can have RAG + interactive)?

### Relationship to V2

V3 RAG support builds directly on several V2 features:
- **`env_vars`** (feature9/10) — RAG agents need API keys for embedding providers and vector store connections
- **Preflight checks** (feature16) — Extended to validate service reachability
- **Trust baseline** (feature17) — Extended to cover lifecycle hooks and data downloads
- **Interactive mode** (feature18+) — RAG agents are often conversational (query → retrieve → answer → follow-up)
- **Per-framework templates** (feature13-15, 19-24) — Extended with `--mode rag` variants
- **Registry** (feature12) — Large archives need size metadata in registry listings

The cleanest path: land V2 fully, then V3 Tier A (embedded RAG) is a relatively contained addition — it's mainly `data` paths in the manifest, data bundling in pack, lifecycle hooks, and new templates.

## Strategic Assessment: Where Kinnoo's Real Value Lives

You're asking the right question at the right time. Let me be direct.

### Where you're right

**Packaging + registry IS the core.** Your own MVP doc says it best: *"If you solve packaging well, everything else (registry, marketplace, deployment, sharing) becomes much easier."* That instinct is correct and well-grounded. The analogy to npm/Docker/pip is apt — nobody remembers those tools for their `npm init` templates. They're remembered because `npm install <thing>` works reliably.

**Runtime as pass-through is correct.** The black-box execution model (`python run.py "<input>"`) is Kinnoo's sharpest design decision. You are right that `kinnoo run` is essentially a managed proxy. The value it adds is **environment setup** (venv, deps, secrets, preflight), not execution logic. Don't let V2 scope creep compromise this.

### Where I need to push back

**You're undervaluing `kinnoo init`, but for the wrong reason.** You frame it as "template library vs. package manager" — as if these are competing directions. They're not. They're different stages of the same funnel:

```
init (CREATE agents) → pack (PACKAGE agents) → publish (SHARE agents) → install + run (USE agents)
```

The problem is: **a registry is useless without supply.** npm didn't succeed because `npm install` was great — it succeeded because millions of developers `npm publish`ed packages. The chicken-and-egg problem for Kinnoo is: who publishes agents to your registry?

`kinnoo init` is your **supply-side tool.** It lowers the barrier for agent creators to produce Kinnoo-compatible packages. Without it (or something like it), you need every agent developer to manually learn your manifest format, directory structure, and conventions. That's friction that kills adoption.

However — and this is where your instinct is partially correct — **the current V2 plan over-invests in init templates.** Having 18 features dedicated to per-framework × per-mode template combinations (features 13-15, 19-24, 27-32) is excessive for a packaging tool. You're right that this starts to look like an "agent template library." The solution isn't to abandon init — it's to make init minimal and convention-driven, and invest disproportionately on the packaging/registry side.

### The strategic lens: what happens in the agent ecosystem in 2026-2027

Here's what I see coming, and what it means for Kinnoo:

**1. Framework convergence around MCP + function calling.** MCP is becoming the standard tool interface. Every major framework (LangGraph, PydanticAI, Agno) now supports MCP natively. This means the "tool layer" is standardizing, which is *good* for Kinnoo — you don't need to understand agent internals. But it also means `kinnoo init` templates become less valuable over time, because frameworks ship their own scaffolding (`langgraph new`, `pydantic-ai init`, etc.).

**2. The "dependency hell" problem for agents is about to explode.** As agents get more complex (RAG pipelines, multi-tool setups, MCP server dependencies, vector stores, embedding models), the number of things that need to "just work" when you install someone else's agent is growing fast. Today's agent tutorials assume you manually install ChromaDB, set up Pinecone, configure API keys — it's the "works on my machine" problem that Docker solved for web services. **This is Kinnoo's real opportunity.**

**3. No one has solved agent distribution yet.** HuggingFace has model distribution. PyPI has library distribution. Docker Hub has container distribution. But there is no broadly adopted standard for "I built an agent, you can install and run it with one command." This gap is widening as agents become multi-component systems (code + prompts + tools + data + secrets + services).

**4. Agent composition is coming.** Agents calling other agents (A2A protocol, multi-agent orchestration) means agents need to be addressable, versioned, and dependency-managed — exactly what a registry provides.

### So what should Kinnoo prioritize?

Here's my recommended strategic hierarchy for V2 and beyond:

| Priority | Capability | Why |
|----------|-----------|-----|
| **1 (highest)** | **Packaging robustness** — transitive deps, reproducible archives, data/asset bundling | Without this, nothing else matters. An agent that doesn't install reliably is worthless. |
| **2** | **Registry** — local first, then remote. Publish, install-by-name, versioning, search | This is the network effect. It's what makes Kinnoo a platform rather than a build tool. |
| **3** | **Dependency declaration** — env vars, services, external connections, preflight checks | The "it just works" factor. Agents need API keys, vector stores, MCP servers. Kinnoo should validate and provision these. |
| **4** | **Inspect + trust** — transparency into what an agent needs before you run it | Security story. Critical for adoption. Nobody will `kinnoo install` an unknown agent without seeing what it does first. |
| **5** | **Init (lightweight)** — basic scaffolding, not per-framework templates | Keep it. But one generic template + maybe 2-3 framework examples is enough. Don't build 18 variants. |
| **6 (lowest for V2)** | **Interactive mode, MCP server packaging, RAG data bundling** | Valuable but not foundational. These are V3 features that build on a solid packaging + registry base. |

### The revised mental model

Instead of:
> Kinnoo = init templates + packaging + runtime + registry

Think:
> Kinnoo = **agent package manager** (like pip/npm for agents)
> 
> Core loop: `pack → publish → install → run`
> 
> Value add: dependency resolution, secret management, reproducibility, trust/transparency

`kinnoo init` is a convenience feature (like `npm init`), not a product pillar. Interactive mode and MCP server support are runtime extensions that should come *after* the package management story is rock-solid.

### What this means for the V2 plan

The current 32-feature V2 plan is **too template-heavy and too broad.** I'd restructure it as:

- **V2:** Packaging robustness + manifest V2 + env vars/secrets + local registry + inspect + trust baseline + 2-3 init templates (not 18). **~12-15 features.**
- **V3:** Interactive mode + MCP support + remote registry + data/asset bundling + RAG support + remaining templates. Build on the solid V2 packaging foundation.

The key question for every V2 feature should be: *"Does this make `kinnoo install <agent> && kinnoo run <agent>` more reliable and trustworthy?"* If yes, it's V2. If it's about agent creation or advanced runtimes, it's V3.

---

### One more thing: the "killer scenario" to design around

---

## What "Packaging Robustness" Actually Means

In V1, `kinnoo pack` works for the happy path: a simple agent with a few pure-Python dependencies. It breaks or produces unreliable archives in several real-world scenarios:

| Problem | What happens today | Impact |
|---------|-------------------|--------|
| **Transitive deps missing** | `pip wheel --no-deps` only bundles direct deps. If `langchain` requires `pydantic`, `pydantic` is NOT in the archive. | Agent fails on install if the machine doesn't have internet or has different versions |
| **Platform-specific wheels** | Wheels built on macOS ARM won't install on Linux x86. No cross-platform handling. | "Works on my machine" — the exact problem Kinnoo exists to solve |
| **No archive integrity** | No checksum or signature on `.kno` files | Can't verify the archive wasn't tampered with. Blocks trust story. |
| **No size awareness** | Pack doesn't warn or report archive size | A LangChain agent with all transitive deps could be 500MB+ of wheels. User has no visibility. |
| **Brittle archive structure** | Some edge cases in zip handling, no canonical layout validation | Install can fail silently on malformed archives |

"Packaging robustness" means fixing these so that `kinnoo pack` produces an archive that **reliably installs and runs on a different machine.** It's not glamorous work, but it's the foundation.

---

## The Version Goals: What Agent Tier Each Version Supports

Here's how I'd frame it — each version should have a clear **target agent archetype** that defines "done":

### V1 (Complete): The Hello World Agent

**Target archetype:** A one-shot LLM agent with a single API provider.

**Example:** "Ask ChatGPT a question and print the answer"
```
Code: run.py (20 lines)
Dependencies: openai
Secrets: OPENAI_API_KEY (manually set by user)
Data: none
External services: none
```

**What V1 proves:** The pack → install → run cycle works end-to-end for the simplest case. The manifest format is viable. The black-box model works.

**What V1 can't do:** Multiple secrets, dependency reliability across machines, discoverability, any agent complexity beyond "call one LLM."

---

### V2 Goal: The Multi-Tool Agent

**Target archetype:** An agent that uses one LLM provider + 2-3 Python-based tools/libraries, with multiple API keys, shareable via a local registry.

**Example:** "A LangChain agent that answers questions using OpenAI, searches the web with Tavily, and checks the weather with a REST API"
```
Code: run.py + tools/ (100-200 lines)
Dependencies: langchain, openai, tavily-python, requests (+ all transitive deps)
Secrets: OPENAI_API_KEY, TAVILY_API_KEY
Data: none
External services: none (all accessed via Python libraries + API keys)
```

**Why this archetype?** This is the most common "real" agent being built today. Tutorials on LangChain, PydanticAI, Agno — they all look like this. An LLM with a few tool integrations, all accessed through Python packages and API keys. No infrastructure to set up. No vector databases. No MCP servers. Just code, deps, and secrets.

**What V2 must solve to support this:**

1. **Reliable dependency bundling** — transitive deps included, cross-platform awareness (at minimum: warn if platform-specific wheels detected)
2. **Secret declaration + injection** — manifest declares `env_vars: [OPENAI_API_KEY, TAVILY_API_KEY]`, runtime resolves from env → .env file → interactive prompt
3. **Local registry** — `kinnoo publish` stores the archive locally, `kinnoo install agent-name` retrieves it. Version management. This is what turns Kinnoo from a build tool into a package manager.
4. **Inspect + preflight** — before running, show what the agent needs (deps, secrets, Python version). Validate everything is present before execution.
5. **Archive integrity** — checksums so you can verify what you installed is what was published

**What V2 explicitly does NOT need:**
- Vector stores or databases
- MCP server dependencies
- Data file bundling
- Interactive/REPL mode
- Remote registry
- Cross-platform wheel compilation (just detection + warning)
- Container/sandbox isolation

**V2 success test:** A developer on Machine A builds a LangChain+Tavily agent, runs `kinnoo pack && kinnoo publish`. A developer on Machine B (same OS) runs `kinnoo install my-agent && kinnoo run my-agent "What's the weather in NYC?"` — it prompts for API keys, installs deps, and runs successfully. Zero manual setup beyond providing secrets.

---

### V3 Goal: The Connected Agent

**Target archetype:** An agent with external service dependencies — vector stores, MCP tool servers, or databases that exist outside the Python process.

**Example:** "A RAG agent that uses LlamaIndex + Pinecone for retrieval, OpenAI for generation, and a GitHub MCP server for code search"
```
Code: run.py + tools/ + prompts/ (300+ lines)
Dependencies: llama-index, openai, pinecone-client (+ transitive)
Secrets: OPENAI_API_KEY, PINECONE_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN
External services: 
  - Pinecone index at env.PINECONE_INDEX_URL
  - GitHub MCP server (stdio or HTTP)
Data: possibly bundled documents for local RAG, or remote-only
```

**What's new vs. V2:** The agent depends on things that aren't just Python packages and API keys. There are **services** that need to be running or reachable. This is a fundamentally harder problem.

**What V3 must solve:**

1. **Service declaration in manifest** — `services:` section that declares external dependencies (vector store type + connection, MCP server reference, database engine)
2. **Preflight service checks** — before running, verify services are reachable (HTTP health check on Pinecone endpoint, MCP server availability)
3. **Data/asset bundling** — optional `data:` section in manifest for bundling documents, embeddings, or pre-built indices in the archive
4. **Lifecycle hooks** — `post_install` script support (e.g., "build the ChromaDB index from bundled documents after install")
5. **MCP server packaging** — an agent that IS an MCP server (long-running process, `runtime.type: mcp-server`)
6. **Remote registry** — for real distribution beyond a single machine. This is where Kinnoo becomes a platform.
7. **Interactive mode** — RAG agents are inherently conversational. REPL support belongs here.

**V3 success test:** The killer scenario from before. Developer A builds a RAG agent with Pinecone + MCP tools, publishes to Kinnoo's remote registry. Developer B runs `kinnoo install rag-agent`, gets prompted for API keys, Kinnoo validates Pinecone is reachable and MCP server is available, and the agent runs a multi-turn conversation.

---

### V4 Goal: The Composable Agent

**Target archetype:** Multi-agent systems where agents depend on other agents, with governance, sandboxing, and enterprise-grade trust.

**Example:** "An orchestrator agent that delegates to a research agent (RAG), a code agent (MCP tools), and a writing agent, all packaged separately and composed via A2A or direct invocation"
```
Agent dependencies: research-agent@1.2.0, code-agent@2.0.0, writer-agent@1.0.0
Orchestration: workflow graph or A2A protocol
Trust: sandboxed execution, permission scoping, audit trail
```

**What V4 must solve:**

1. **Agent-as-dependency** — manifest declares dependencies on other Kinnoo agents, with version constraints
2. **Agent composition** — an agent can invoke another installed agent (sub-process, API, or A2A)
3. **Sandboxed execution** — container-based isolation for untrusted agents
4. **Permission model** — declare and enforce what an agent can access (network, filesystem, other agents)
5. **Audit/governance** — execution traces, cost tracking, approval workflows for sensitive actions
6. **Multi-language support** — agents in Node.js, Go, etc. (not just Python)

**V4 success test:** An enterprise team deploys a multi-agent system where each agent is independently versioned, published, and sandboxed. Updating one agent doesn't break the others. Permissions are enforced at the Kinnoo level.

---

## The Progression at a Glance

| Version | Target Agent | Key Capability Added | Tagline |
|---------|-------------|---------------------|---------|
| **V1** ✅ | One-shot, single LLM | Pack → Install → Run | "Package any agent. Run it anywhere." |
| **V2** | Multi-tool, multi-secret | Reliable deps + secrets + local registry | "Install any agent. It just works." |
| **V3** | Connected (RAG, MCP, services) | Service deps + data + remote registry | "Share any agent. Run it with its full stack." |
| **V4** | Composable multi-agent | Agent-as-dependency + sandboxing | "Compose agents. Trust them. Scale them." |

---

## Answering Your Direct Question

> Would I be able to support the RAG+ChromaDB+Pinecone+MCP agent in V2?

**No, and you shouldn't try.** That agent has external service dependencies (Pinecone, MCP servers) that require service declaration, health checks, and possibly data bundling. That's V3 territory.

> What's the minimum agent V2 should fully support?

**A multi-tool agent with multiple Python dependencies and multiple API keys, discoverable via a local registry.** This is the 80% case for agents being built today. It's a meaningful step up from V1, it's achievable, and it forces you to solve the hard packaging problems (transitive deps, secrets, registry) without the complexity of external services.

> What's the "goal" of V2?

**Make `kinnoo install <agent> && kinnoo run <agent>` reliable and trustworthy for any Python-based agent whose dependencies are pip-installable packages and API keys.** Every V2 feature should serve that goal. If a feature doesn't make install+run more reliable for this class of agent, it's not V2.

The black-box model works.\n\n**What V1 can't do:** Multiple secrets, dependency reliability across machines, discoverability, any agent complexity beyond \"call one LLM.\"\n\n---\n\n### V2 Goal: The Multi-Tool Agent\n\n**Target archetype:** An agent that uses one LLM provider + 2-3 Python-based tools/libraries, with multiple API keys, shareable via a local registry.\n\n**Example:** \"A LangChain agent that answers questions using OpenAI, searches the web with Tavily, and checks the weather with a REST API\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nCode: run.py + tools/ (100-200 lines)\nDependencies: langchain, openai, tavily-python, requests (+ all transitive deps)\nSecrets: OPENAI_API_KEY, TAVILY_API_KEY\nData: none\nExternal services: none (all accessed via Python libraries + API keys)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Why this archetype?** This is the most common \"real\" agent being built today. Tutorials on LangChain, PydanticAI, Agno — they all look like this. An LLM with a few tool integrations, all accessed through Python packages and API keys. No infrastructure to set up. No vector databases. No MCP servers. Just code, deps, and secrets.\n\n**What V2 must solve to support this:**\n\n1. **Reliable dependency bundling** — transitive deps included, cross-platform awareness (at minimum: warn if platform-specific wheels detected)\n2. **Secret declaration + injection** — manifest declares &#96;env_vars: [OPENAI_API_KEY, TAVILY_API_KEY]&#96;, runtime resolves from env → .env file → interactive prompt\n3. **Local registry** — &#96;kinnoo publish&#96; stores the archive locally, &#96;kinnoo install agent-name&#96; retrieves it. Version management. This is what turns Kinnoo from a build tool into a package manager.\n4. **Inspect + preflight** — before running, show what the agent needs (deps, secrets, Python version). Validate everything is present before execution.\n5. **Archive integrity** — checksums so you can verify what you installed is what was published\n\n**What V2 explicitly does NOT need:**\n- Vector stores or databases\n- MCP server dependencies\n- Data file bundling\n- Interactive/REPL mode\n- Remote registry\n- Cross-platform wheel compilation (just detection + warning)\n- Container/sandbox isolation\n\n**V2 success test:** A developer on Machine A builds a LangChain+Tavily agent, runs &#96;kinnoo pack &amp;&amp; kinnoo publish&#96;. A developer on Machine B (same OS) runs &#96;kinnoo install my-agent &amp;&amp; kinnoo run my-agent \"What's the weather in NYC?\"&#96; — it prompts for API keys, installs deps, and runs successfully. Zero manual setup beyond providing secrets.\n\n---\n\n### V3 Goal: The Connected Agent\n\n**Target archetype:** An agent with external service dependencies — vector stores, MCP tool servers, or databases that exist outside the Python process.\n\n**Example:** \"A RAG agent that uses LlamaIndex + Pinecone for retrieval, OpenAI for generation, and a GitHub MCP server for code search\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nCode: run.py + tools/ + prompts/ (300+ lines)\nDependencies: llama-index, openai, pinecone-client (+ transitive)\nSecrets: OPENAI_API_KEY, PINECONE_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN\nExternal services: \n  - Pinecone index at env.PINECONE_INDEX_URL\n  - GitHub MCP server (stdio or HTTP)\nData: possibly bundled documents for local RAG, or remote-only\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**What's new vs. V2:** The agent depends on things that aren't just Python packages and API keys. There are **services** that need to be running or reachable. This is a fundamentally harder problem.\n\n**What V3 must solve:**\n\n1. **Service declaration in manifest** — &#96;services:&#96; section that declares external dependencies (vector store type + connection, MCP server reference, database engine)\n2. **Preflight service checks** — before running, verify services are reachable (HTTP health check on Pinecone endpoint, MCP server availability)\n3. **Data/asset bundling** — optional &#96;data:&#96; section in manifest for bundling documents, embeddings, or pre-built indices in the archive\n4. **Lifecycle hooks** — &#96;post_install&#96; script support (e.g., \"build the ChromaDB index from bundled documents after install\")\n5. **MCP server packaging** — an agent that IS an MCP server (long-running process, &#96;runtime.type: mcp-server&#96;)\n6. **Remote registry** — for real distribution beyond a single machine. This is where Kinnoo becomes a platform.\n7. **Interactive mode** — RAG agents are inherently conversational. REPL support belongs here.\n\n**V3 success test:** The killer scenario from before. Developer A builds a RAG agent with Pinecone + MCP tools, publishes to Kinnoo's remote registry. Developer B runs &#96;kinnoo install rag-agent&#96;, gets prompted for API keys, Kinnoo validates Pinecone is reachable and MCP server is available, and the agent runs a multi-turn conversation.\n\n---\n\n### V4 Goal: The Composable Agent\n\n**Target archetype:** Multi-agent systems where agents depend on other agents, with governance, sandboxing, and enterprise-grade trust.\n\n**Example:** \"An orchestrator agent that delegates to a research agent (RAG), a code agent (MCP tools), and a writing agent, all packaged separately and composed via A2A or direct invocation\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nAgent dependencies: research-agent@1.2.0, code-agent@2.0.0, writer-agent@1.0.0\nOrchestration: workflow graph or A2A protocol\nTrust: sandboxed execution, permission scoping, audit trail\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**What V4 must solve:**\n\n1. **Agent-as-dependency** — manifest declares dependencies on other Kinnoo agents, with version constraints\n2. **Agent composition** — an agent can invoke another installed agent (sub-process, API, or A2A)\n3. **Sandboxed execution** — container-based isolation for untrusted agents\n4. **Permission model** — declare and enforce what an agent can access (network, filesystem, other agents)\n5. **Audit/governance** — execution traces, cost tracking, approval workflows for sensitive actions\n6. **Multi-language support** — agents in Node.js, Go, etc. (not just Python)\n\n**V4 success test:** An enterprise team deploys a multi-agent system where each agent is independently versioned, published, and sandboxed. Updating one agent doesn't break the others. Permissions are enforced at the Kinnoo level.\n\n---\n\n## The Progression at a Glance\n\n| Version | Target Agent | Key Capability Added | Tagline |\n|---------|-------------|---------------------|---------|\n| **V1** ✅ | One-shot, single LLM | Pack → Install → Run | \"Package any agent. Run it anywhere.\" |\n| **V2** | Multi-tool, multi-secret | Reliable deps + secrets + local registry | \"Install any agent. It just works.\" |\n| **V3** | Connected (RAG, MCP, services) | Service deps + data + remote registry | \"Share any agent. Run it with its full stack.\" |\n| **V4** | Composable multi-agent | Agent-as-dependency + sandboxing | \"Compose agents. Trust them. Scale them.\" |\n\n---\n\n## Answering Your Direct Question\n\n&gt; Would I be able to support the RAG+ChromaDB+Pinecone+MCP agent in V2?\n\n**No, and you shouldn't try.** That agent has external service dependencies (Pinecone, MCP servers) that require service declaration, health checks, and possibly data bundling. That's V3 territory.\n\n&gt; What's the minimum agent V2 should fully support?\n\n**A multi-tool agent with multiple Python dependencies and multiple API keys, discoverable via a local registry.** This is the 80% case for agents being built today. It's a meaningful step up from V1, it's achievable, and it forces you to solve the hard packaging problems (transitive deps, secrets, registry) without the complexity of external services.\n\n&gt; What's the \"goal\" of V2?\n\n**Make &#96;kinnoo install &lt;agent&gt; &amp;&amp; kinnoo run &lt;agent&gt;&#96; reliable and trustworthy for any Python-based agent whose dependencies are pip-installable packages and API keys.** Every V2 feature should serve that goal. If a feature doesn't make install+run more reliable for this class of agent, it's not V2.\n",

## Plan: Revised V2 Feature List

**TL;DR:** 10 features (feature7–feature16), focused exclusively on making `kinnoo install <agent> && kinnoo run <agent>` reliable and trustworthy for multi-tool, multi-secret Python agents. All template, interactive, and MCP features moved to V3. Every feature passes the filter: "Does this make install+run more reliable?"

### Overview Table

| ID | Title | Tier | Depends On | Effort | V2 Goal Justification |
|----|-------|------|------------|--------|----------------------|
| **Tier 1: Foundation (tech debt)** | | | | | |
| feature7 | CLI Refactor & Modular Architecture | 1 | — | Small | Unlocks all V2 work; fixes V1 hacks |
| feature8 | Packaging Robustness | 1 | — | Medium | THE core V2 problem — transitive deps, reliable archives |
| feature9 | Manifest Schema V2 Extensions | 1 | — | Small | Enables env_vars, metadata for registry/inspect |
| **Tier 2: Core ("it just works")** | | | | | |
| feature10 | Environment Variable / Secret Management | 2 | feature9 | Medium | Multi-secret agents need automated resolution |
| feature11 | `kinnoo inspect` Command | 2 | feature7 | Small | Transparency — see what an agent needs before install/run |
| feature12 | Local Registry | 2 | feature11 | Medium | Core package manager: publish, install-by-name, versioning |
| **Tier 3: Trust & Reliability** | | | | | |
| feature13 | Preflight Checks (`--preflight`) | 3 | feature10 | Medium | Validate everything before execution — "it just works" |
| feature14 | Trust Baseline | 3 | feature10 | Small | Install transparency, unverified source warnings, run logging |
| feature15 | Archive Integrity (Checksums) | 3 | feature8 | Small | Verify archives haven't been tampered with |
| feature16 | Pack Size Reporting & Warnings | 3 | feature8 | Small | Visibility into archive size; warn on large packs |

### Feature Details

---

#### feature7 — CLI Refactor & Modular Architecture

Extract install logic from monolithic `cli.py` into a dedicated `install_command.py` module (matching `init_command.py` and `pack_command.py`). Add `--version` flag. Clean up duplicate test in test_pack.py.

**ACs:**
1. Install logic lives in `src/kinnoo/install_command.py`, not inline in `cli.py`
2. `cli.py` imports and delegates to `install_command.py` for install operations
3. `kinnoo --version` prints the package version and exits
4. No duplicate test functions exist in the test suite
5. All existing V1 tests continue to pass after refactor

---

#### feature8 — Packaging Robustness

Fix transitive dependency bundling in `kinnoo pack` (currently uses `--no-deps`). Canonicalize archive format as zip. Implement fallback behavior for missing/failed wheel builds. Add cross-platform wheel detection with warnings.

**ACs:**
1. `kinnoo pack` includes transitive dependencies (not just direct), so `pip install` in an offline venv succeeds
2. Archive format is zip with `.kno` extension; all docs/code/notes reference zip consistently
3. If a wheel build fails for a dependency, `kinnoo pack` warns but continues (does not abort the entire pack)
4. `kinnoo install` falls back to PyPI install for any missing wheels (with a warning message)
5. A packed agent with transitive deps installs and runs correctly in a fresh venv with no internet access (offline install test)
6. If platform-specific wheels are detected during packing, a warning is printed: "Archive contains platform-specific wheels that may not install on other operating systems"

---

#### feature9 — Manifest Schema V2 Extensions

Add optional fields to `kinnoo.yaml` schema: `description`, `author`, `license`, `env_vars` (list[string]). All additions are non-breaking — existing V1 manifests remain valid.

**ACs:**
1. `description` (string), `author` (string), `license` (string) are accepted as optional fields; absent is valid
2. `env_vars` (list[string]) is accepted as an optional field; validator ensures it is a list of strings when present
3. A V1 manifest (without any new fields) still passes validation with no errors
4. Invalid types for new fields (e.g., `env_vars` as a string, `description` as a number) produce specific error messages naming the field and expected type
5. `kinnoo init` templates include `description` and `author` fields with placeholder values
6. `env_vars` items are validated as non-empty strings (no empty string items in the list)

**Note:** `runtime.type` list support (for interactive, mcp-server) is deferred to V3 since those runtime modes are V3 features. V2 keeps `runtime.type` as a single string with only `one-shot` as a valid value.

---

#### feature10 — Environment Variable / Secret Management (`env_vars`)

When running an agent whose `kinnoo.yaml` declares `env_vars`, the runtime checks, resolves, and injects the required variables into the subprocess environment. Resolution order: current environment → `.env` file in agent directory → interactive prompt. **Secret values must NEVER be displayed, logged, or echoed anywhere in the codebase.**

**ACs:**
1. If `env_vars` declares variables and all are set in the current environment, agent runs normally with those vars injected into the subprocess
2. If a declared env var is missing from environment, kinnoo checks for a `.env` file in the agent directory and loads matching variables
3. If a declared env var is still missing after `.env` check, kinnoo prompts the user interactively with **masked input** (characters not echoed to terminal)
4. All resolved env vars are injected into the subprocess environment when executing the agent
5. If the user declines to provide a missing env var (e.g., Ctrl+C), execution aborts with a clear message listing which variable was not provided
6. Agents without `env_vars` in manifest are unaffected — no prompting, no `.env` loading, existing V1 behavior unchanged
7. **No code path in the entire codebase ever prints, logs, or displays the VALUE of any env var or secret** — only variable NAMES may appear in output or logs

---

#### feature11 — `kinnoo inspect` Command

New CLI command that reads and displays manifest metadata from a `.kno` archive or agent directory. Provides transparency into what an agent requires before install/run.

**ACs:**
1. `kinnoo inspect <agent-dir>` reads `kinnoo.yaml` and displays: name, version, description, author, license, dependencies, env_var NAMES (not values), runtime type
2. `kinnoo inspect <archive.kno>` reads manifest from inside the zip archive without extracting the full archive to disk
3. Output is human-readable formatted text (not raw YAML dump)
4. Missing optional fields are omitted from output (not shown as "None" or empty)
5. Invalid manifest produces a clear error (reuses feature1 validator)
6. `kinnoo inspect` without arguments prints usage help

---

#### feature12 — Local Registry (`kinnoo publish`, `kinnoo install <name>`, `kinnoo list`, `kinnoo search`)

Implement a local registry at `~/.kinnoo/registry/` where agents can be published by name/version and installed by name. Version is extracted from the archive's `kinnoo.yaml`. Code is structured behind an abstraction so swapping to a remote backend in V3 is straightforward.

**ACs:**
1. `kinnoo publish <archive.kno>` extracts name and version from the archive's `kinnoo.yaml` and copies the archive to `~/.kinnoo/registry/<name>/<version>/`
2. `kinnoo publish <archive.kno> --local` does the same (explicit local flag for forward-compatibility)
3. `kinnoo install <name>` resolves the latest version from local registry and installs it (no network required)
4. `kinnoo install <name>==<version>` installs a specific version from local registry
5. `kinnoo list` displays all locally published agents with name, latest version, and description
6. `kinnoo search <query>` filters the local registry by name/description substring match
7. Publishing the same name+version twice produces a clear error (no silent overwrite)
8. `kinnoo install <file.kno>` (file path) continues to work as before (V1 behavior preserved)
9. Publish/resolve logic is behind an abstraction (e.g., `RegistryBackend` interface) so swapping local for remote is a minimal change

---

#### feature13 — Preflight Checks (`--preflight`)

Add `--preflight` flag to `kinnoo run` that validates the agent's environment before execution. Catches missing deps, wrong Python version, missing secrets — gives actionable guidance instead of cryptic runtime errors.

**ACs:**
1. `kinnoo run <dir> --preflight` runs all checks and reports results **without executing the agent**
2. Check: Python version matches `runtime.version` constraint in manifest
3. Check: All declared `env_vars` NAMES are resolvable (set in env or in `.env` file) — **never displays values**
4. Check: Entrypoint file exists at the declared path
5. Check: All dependencies in `requirements.txt` are installed in the venv (or installable)
6. Results are printed as a checklist with pass/fail status for each check
7. If all checks pass, prints "Ready to run"; if any fail, prints actionable guidance per failed check

---

#### feature14 — Trust Baseline

Add transparency and trust features: display dependency/secret summary on install, warn on untrusted source agents, and log run traces. **Absolute rule: no env var or secret VALUES ever appear in output, logs, or code paths.**

**ACs:**
1. `kinnoo install` displays a summary of what the agent requires (env_var NAMES, dependency NAMES, runtime type) before installing, and prompts for yes/no confirmation
2. If an agent is installed from a raw `.kno` file (not from the local registry), a warning is displayed: "This agent is from an unverified source"
3. `kinnoo run` logs a trace to `~/.kinnoo/logs/run.log` containing ONLY: timestamp, agent name, runtime type, and exit code — **no input content, no env var values, no secrets**
4. `kinnoo run` displays the agent's declared env_var NAMES and dependency NAMES before first execution (first run only) — **never values**
5. Log file never contains actual values of environment variables, secrets, or user input
6. All trust-related display and logging code includes inline comments documenting the "no secret values" invariant

---

#### feature15 — Archive Integrity (Checksums)

Generate and verify SHA256 checksums for `.kno` archives. Enables detection of tampered or corrupted archives.

**ACs:**
1. `kinnoo pack` generates a `.kno.sha256` checksum file alongside the `.kno` archive
2. `kinnoo install <file.kno>` checks for a `.kno.sha256` file; if present, verifies the archive matches before extracting
3. If checksum verification fails, install aborts with a clear error: "Archive integrity check failed — the file may be corrupted or tampered with"
4. If no `.kno.sha256` file is present, install proceeds with a warning: "No checksum file found — archive integrity not verified"
5. `kinnoo publish` stores the checksum alongside the archive in the registry
6. `kinnoo inspect` displays the archive checksum if available

---

#### feature16 — Pack Size Reporting & Warnings

Report archive size after packing and warn when archives are unusually large (common with heavy dependency trees like LangChain).

**ACs:**
1. `kinnoo pack` prints the final archive size in human-readable format (e.g., "Archive size: 45.2 MB") after packing
2. If archive size exceeds 100MB, a warning is printed: "Warning: archive is large (X MB). Consider whether all dependencies are necessary."
3. `kinnoo inspect` displays the archive size when inspecting a `.kno` file
4. `kinnoo list` includes archive size in the registry listing

---

### What Moved to V3

These features from the previous 32-feature plan are deferred to V3 per the strategic alignment:

| Deferred Feature | Reason |
|-----------------|--------|
| All interactive mode features (18-24) | Runtime extension, not packaging. V3 target: "Connected Agent" |
| All MCP features (25-32) | Advanced runtime, not packaging. V3 target: "Connected Agent" |
| Per-framework one-shot templates (pydantic-ai, langgraph, agno) | Agent creation, not packaging. `kinnoo init` is convenience, not core |
| `runtime.type` list support | Not needed until interactive/mcp modes exist in V3 |
| Run from archive directly | Convenience, not reliability |

### V2 Success Test (restated)

A developer on Machine A builds a LangChain+Tavily agent (multi-tool, multi-secret), runs:
```bash
kinnoo pack ./my-agent && kinnoo publish ./my-agent-1.0.0.kno
```

A developer on Machine B (same OS) runs:
```bash
kinnoo install my-agent
# → displays deps + env_var names, prompts for confirmation
# → installs from local registry
kinnoo run ./my-agent "What's the weather in NYC?"
# → prompts for OPENAI_API_KEY, TAVILY_API_KEY (masked input)
# → runs agent successfully
```

Zero manual setup beyond providing secrets. Every feature in this list serves that scenario.

### Decisions Log

- **Reduced from 32 features to 10.** Applied the filter: "Does this make install+run more reliable?" ruthlessly.
- **All template features moved to V3.** `kinnoo init` is convenience, not core packaging. Existing V1 templates (gemini, chatgpt, claude-chat) are sufficient for V2.
- **All interactive/MCP features moved to V3.** These are runtime extensions for the "Connected Agent" archetype.
- **Added feature15 (Archive Integrity) and feature16 (Size Reporting).** These were identified in the packaging robustness analysis but weren't in the previous plan. They directly serve trust and reliability.
- **`runtime.type` stays single-string in V2.** List support deferred until V3 interactive/mcp modes need it.
- **Kept env_vars naming** — industry-appropriate for "list of variable names."
- **No `--force` flag** — safety first, consistent with V1 decision.

Provides transparency into what an agent requires before install or run.\n      Displays env_var names (never values), dependencies, runtime type, and other metadata.\n    tasks: []\n    acceptance_criteria:\n      - id: AC1\n        description: \"&#96;kinnoo inspect &lt;agent-dir&gt;&#96; reads kinnoo.yaml and displays: name, version, description, author, license, dependencies, env_var NAMES (not values), and runtime type.\"\n      - id: AC2\n        description: \"&#96;kinnoo inspect &lt;archive.kno&gt;&#96; reads the manifest from inside the zip archive without extracting the full archive to disk.\"\n      - id: AC3\n        description: \"Output is human-readable formatted text (not a raw YAML dump).\"\n      - id: AC4\n        description: \"Missing optional fields are omitted from output (not shown as None or empty).\"\n      - id: AC5\n        description: \"Invalid manifest produces a clear error (reuses feature1 validator).\"\n      - id: AC6\n        description: \"&#96;kinnoo inspect&#96; without arguments prints usage help.\"\n    owner: techlead-agent\n    dependencies: [feature7]\n    status: not-started\n\n  - id: feature12\n    title: \"Local Registry (kinnoo publish, kinnoo install &lt;name&gt;, kinnoo list, kinnoo search)\"\n    description: |\n      Implement a local registry at ~/.kinnoo/registry/ where agents can be published by\n      name/version and installed by name. Version is extracted from the archive's kinnoo.yaml.\n      Publish and resolve logic is structured behind an abstraction so swapping to a remote\n      backend in V3 requires minimal changes.\n    tasks: []\n    acceptance_criteria:\n      - id: AC1\n        description: \"&#96;kinnoo publish &lt;archive.kno&gt;&#96; extracts name and version from the archive's kinnoo.yaml and copies the archive to ~/.kinnoo/registry/&lt;name&gt;/&lt;version&gt;/.\"\n      - id: AC2\n        description: \"&#96;kinnoo publish &lt;archive.kno&gt; --local&#96; does the same as AC1 (explicit local flag for forward-compatibility).\"\n      - id: AC3\n        description: \"&#96;kinnoo install &lt;name&gt;&#96; resolves the latest version from the local registry and installs it with no network required.\"\n      - id: AC4\n        description: \"&#96;kinnoo install &lt;name&gt;==&lt;version&gt;&#96; installs a specific version from the local registry.\"\n      - id: AC5\n        description: \"&#96;kinnoo list&#96; displays all locally published agents with name, latest version, and description.\"\n      - id: AC6\n        description: \"&#96;kinnoo search &lt;query&gt;&#96; filters the local registry by name/description substring match.\"\n      - id: AC7\n        description: \"Publishing the same name+version twice produces a clear error (no silent overwrite).\"\n      - id: AC8\n        description: \"&#96;kinnoo install &lt;file.kno&gt;&#96; (file path) continues to work as before (V1 behavior preserved).\"\n      - id: AC9\n        description: \"Publish/resolve logic is behind an abstraction (e.g., RegistryBackend interface) so swapping local for remote backend is a minimal change.\"\n    owner: techlead-agent\n    dependencies: [feature11]\n    status: not-started\n\n  - id: feature13\n    title: \"Preflight Checks (--preflight flag on kinnoo run)\"\n    description: |\n      Add a --preflight flag to &#96;kinnoo run&#96; Absolute rule:\n      no env var or secret VALUES ever appear in output, logs, or code paths — only names.\n    tasks: []\n    acceptance_criteria:\n      - id: AC1\n        description: \"&#96;kinnoo install&#96; displays a summary of what the agent requires (env_var NAMES, dependency NAMES, runtime type) before installing and prompts for yes/no confirmation.\"\n      - id: AC2\n        description: \"If an agent is installed from a raw .kno file (not from the local registry), a warning is displayed: 'This agent is from an unverified source'.\"\n      - id: AC3\n        description: \"&#96;kinnoo run&#96; logs a trace to ~/.kinnoo/logs/run.log containing ONLY: timestamp, agent name, runtime type, and exit code — no input content, no env var values, no secrets.\"\n      - id: AC4\n        description: \"&#96;kinnoo run&#96; displays the agent's declared env_var NAMES and dependency NAMES before first execution (first run only) — never values.\"\n      - id: AC5\n        description: \"Log file never contains actual values of environment variables, secrets, or user input.\"\n      - id: AC6\n        description: \"All trust-related display and logging code includes inline comments documenting the 'no secret values' invariant.\"\n    owner: techlead-agent\n    dependencies: [feature10]\n    status: not-started\n\n  - id: feature15\n    title: \"Archive Integrity (Checksums)\"\n    description: |\n      Generate and verify SHA256 checksums for .kno archives. _**User (2026-02-27 16:19Z)**_

Because of these factors:
1. agents will be getting more and more complex
2. frameworks will continue to change and evolve very rapidly, and new frameworks will emerge
3. my platform's one-liner is "package any agent, run it anywhere"
Is there a danger that my platform won't work for a lot of agents, and will constantly break because of new updates? In other words, would I always be trying to play "catch up" to support agent packaging?
